text:
Situation: Dobutamine hydrochloride has been on the FDA shortage list since 2017-11-06 and remains Current as of 2026-10-21. Corvale East holds 3.1 days of 100 mg/100 mL 250 mL bags and 1.7 days of 12.5 mg/mL 20 mL vials. Corvale General holds 25 days of 100 mg/100 mL 250 mL bags, 23.4 days of 400 mg/100 mL, and 14 days of 12.5 mg/mL. Corvale Lakeside holds 13.6 days of 100 mg/100 mL 250 mL bags.

Why (FDA record): FDA first posted the shortage 2017-11-06; status is Current as of 2026-10-21. Inspection 1031233 at Baxter Healthcare Corporation FEI 1416980 ended 2017-10-27 with VAI classification. A later inspection at the same plant ended 2026-04-02 with OAI classification; a Warning Letter was issued 2026-09-29. Hospira, Inc. (a Pfizer Company) is also listed Current for dobutamine hydrochloride.

Our position: Internal transfer is the fastest way to protect Corvale East without new purchasing risk. Alternate concentrations from Hospira and Baxter are FDA-listed Current and have prior clinical approvals.

Recommended actions:
1. Transfer 57 bags of 100 mg/100 mL 250 mL from Corvale General to Corvale East — approved by pharmacy director (transfer request).
2. Evaluate purchase from Hikma Pharmaceuticals USA Inc. — approved by buyer.
3. Use Hospira 12.5 mg/mL vial per existing approval by Sam Rivera, MD (2026-03-20) — pharmacist verification required.
4. Use Baxter 100 mg/100 mL bag per existing approval by Jordan Hale, PharmD (2026-08-14) — pharmacist verification required.

Not recommended: Delaying transfer while awaiting new supplier qualification; relying solely on Lakeside stock without a redistribution plan.
